title: Bug Bounty Methodology
summary: Learn scope-first recon, evidence quality, impact validation, and responsible reporting.

lessons.title: Scope, rules, and evidence quality
lessons.content: Read program scope and exclusions before testing. Prefer minimal proof, avoid collecting other users’ data, stop when impact is established, and report clear reproduction steps with remediation recommendations.

quiz.question: When should a tester stop validating an issue?
options: Only after downloading all accessible data
Never; continue until the system fails
quiz.explanation: Stop once sufficient safe evidence demonstrates impact; avoid unnecessary access or disruption.

lessons.title: Clear reproduction steps and responsible disclosure
lessons.content: An effective report provides immediate business impact, explicit steps to reproduce, HTTP request/response proofs of concept, and pragmatic mitigation advice. Timely communication and coordinated disclosure protect both defenders and users.

quiz.question: What is the most critical element of a high-value bug report?
options: An aggressive tone demanding bounty payment
Clear, minimal reproduction steps demonstrating tangible impact
A dump of automated scanner logs
quiz.explanation: Security teams need clear, deterministic steps to reproduce and verify the underlying impact.
